elements.element: Customer has a right to terminate for convenience
elements.evidence: "Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience"

elements.element: Notice period of 30 days, in writing
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor"

elements.element: Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on such termination
elements.evidence: "Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination"

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: "Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a term."
redline gives "thirty (30) days' prior written notice" (better than fallback, but not the fallback bargain)

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: no early-termination fee; instead "Customer shall have no further payment or minimum-commitment obligation"

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at end of a term on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "Vendor has no right to terminate ... for convenience during a term" — no end-of-term Vendor right granted

offending_extra_words: and Customer shall have no further payment or minimum-commitment obligation for the terminated Services
reasons: All four atomic elements of the preferred position are expressly met: a Customer-only convenience right, 30 days' written notice, refund of prepaid Fees for the post-termination period (pro-rata in substance), and an express bar on Vendor convenience termination during a term.
Fallback is not satisfied as a standalone bargain (30 rather than 60–90 days, no early-termination fee, no end-of-term Vendor right), which is immaterial because the locked target level is preferred.

Minimality fails on three points: the added waiver of "further payment or minimum-commitment obligation" is protection beyond the preferred position (which asks only for a pro-rata refund); "in whole or in part" broadens scope unnecessarily; and the lead-in "Notwithstanding Section 2.1" cross-references a provision not shown in the operative text (the term provision is rendered as 8.1), creating cross-reference risk.

Suggested tightening: "Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination. Vendor may not terminate for convenience during a term."
Unrelated termination rights (9.1–9.3, 9.5) and the three-year term remain untouched and effective.
